name: Question 3
problem:
The second-order differential equation 

$$
{y}^{″}-3t{y}^{′}+{t}^{2}y=6
$$

can be written as a system of first-order differential equations, as follows:

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}={x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}^{′}=f(t)\end{aligned}
$$

where ${x}_{1}(t)=y(t)$ and ${x}_{2}(t)={y}^{′}(t).$ Find the function $f(t).$
worked_solution:
First, we make the following change of variables:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(t) & =y \\ {x}_{2}(t) & ={y}^{′}\end{aligned}
$$

Differentiating the above equations with respect to $t,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t) & ={y}^{′} \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t) & ={y}^{″}\end{aligned}
$$

which we can rewrite as 

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}={x}_{2}, \\ {x}_{2}^{′}={y}^{″}.\end{aligned}
$$

At this point, we're almost done. We just need to write the right-hand side of the last equation in terms of ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}.$

Solving our original differential equation for the highest-order derivative $({y}^{″}),$ we obtain

$$
{y}^{″}=3t{y}^{′}-{t}^{2}y+6.
$$

Then, we substitute our new variables into the right-hand side of the above equation. This gives

$$
{y}^{″}=3t{x}_{2}-{t}^{2}{x}_{1}+6.
$$

Notice that we do not include any derivative terms on the right-hand side. 

Therefore, our complete system of equations is as follows:

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}={x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}^{′}=-{t}^{2}{x}_{1}+3t{x}_{2}+6\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
f(t)=-{t}^{2}{x}_{1}+3t{x}_{2}+6.
$$

Question 3

The second-order differential equation y″−3ty′+t2y=6 can be written as a system of first-order differential equations, as follows: {x1′=x2x2′=f(t) where x1(t)=y(t) and x2(t)=y′(t). Find the function f(t).

a
−t2x1+3tx2+6
b
−t2x1−3tx2−6
c
−3tx1+t2x2+6
d
t2x1−3tx2−6
e
3tx1−t2x2−6
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we make the following change of variables: x1(t)=yx2(t)=y′

Differentiating the above equations with respect to t, we get x1′(t)=y′x2′(t)=y″

which we can rewrite as {x1′=x2,x2′=y″.

At this point, we're almost done. We just need to write the right-hand side of the last equation in terms of x1 and x2.

Solving our original differential equation for the highest-order derivative (y″), we obtain y″=3ty′−t2y+6.

Then, we substitute our new variables into the right-hand side of the above equation. This gives y″=3tx2−t2x1+6. Notice that we do not include any derivative terms on the right-hand side.

Therefore, our complete system of equations is as follows: {x1′=x2x2′=−t2x1+3tx2+6

Finally, f(t)=−t2x1+3tx2+6.
